s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive unilateral facial weakness with associated neurological symptoms
salient_findings: Slight slant of mouth corners towards left
Disappearance of nasolabial fold in right face
key_facts: Lesion located in dorsolateral right pons on brain MRI
No hyper-intense signals in diffusion-weighted images
No vertebrobasilar artery main trunk occlusion or stenosis on MRTA
Significantly decreased amplitude of right facial nerve compound muscular action potential on ENoG
Presence of insertional activity in right facial muscles with greatly reduced voluntary activity on EMG

shortlist.label: Ramsay Hunt syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Unilateral facial weakness and associated neurological symptoms such as hearing loss and diplopia

shortlist.label: Acoustic neuroma
shortlist.why_kept: Unilateral facial weakness and hearing loss, with a lesion located in the dorsolateral right pons on brain MRI

shortlist.label: Facial nerve schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Unilateral facial weakness and a lesion located in the dorsolateral right pons on brain MRI

shortlist.label: Brainstem glioma
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive unilateral facial weakness and a lesion located in the dorsolateral right pons on brain MRI

shortlist.label: Pontine stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Sudden onset of unilateral facial weakness and associated neurological symptoms, with a lesion located in the dorsolateral right pons on brain MRI

raw.rationale: The lesion located in the dorsolateral right pons on brain MRI, along with the patient's symptoms of dizziness, right-sided hearing drop, diplopia, and facial muscle weakness, are consistent with a pontine stroke. The absence of hyper-intense signals in diffusion-weighted images does not rule out a stroke, as the timing of the MRI may not have been optimal for detection.

rejected.label: Ramsay Hunt syndrome
rejected.why: Typically presents with a rash and pain in the ear, which are not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Acoustic neuroma
rejected.why: Would likely cause more prominent hearing loss and tinnitus, and the MRI findings do not suggest a tumor at the cerebellopontine angle

rejected.label: Facial nerve schwannoma
rejected.why: Would likely cause more gradual onset of symptoms and the MRI findings do not suggest a tumor along the facial nerve

rejected.label: Brainstem glioma
rejected.why: Would likely cause more gradual onset of symptoms and the MRI findings do not suggest a glioma, which would typically have a more heterogeneous appearance
